statement: An array of distinct integers was sorted in ascending order and then rotated at some unknown pivot, so it now looks like [nums[k], …, nums[n − 1], nums[0], …, nums[k − 1]]. For example, [0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7] rotated at index 3 becomes [4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2].
You are given the rotated array nums and an integer target. Return the index of target in nums, or −1 if it is not there.
The search must run in O(log n) time. At every midpoint at least one of the two halves is still sorted; check whether target lies inside that sorted half to decide which half to keep.

examples.explanation: 3 is at index 4 of the rotated array.
10 is larger than every element, so it is not in the array and the answer is −1.

constraints: All values of nums are distinct
nums is an ascending array that is possibly rotated
